summary: Recovered the Primary Chat state-compiler runtime binding and enforced the actual CURRENT owner rather than the stale predecessor surface. The served canary index loads current-tree/control-v11/chat-canary/progress-v1.js and does not load current-first-v1.js. The bound compiler derives liveness from durable claim/route/event/close timestamps with a freshness threshold; terminal rows are not live; fresh transport blocks are time-bounded; projection age comes from live/runtime.json + claim-frontier generated_at; QA is only explicit durable metadata. Its contract precedence correctly requires a live worker before RETURNS_UNCONSUMED or RECOVERY_PRESSURE can suppress capacity refill, and its built-in harness explicitly covers returns/recovery with zero live workers -> REFILL_N. Added a deterministic static regression primary_chat_state_runtime_binding_v1.mjs that locks the actual index->progress binding, durable-liveness predicates, no-live-consumer refill cases and NON_AUTHORITATIVE_DERIVED_PROJECTION authority. Wired that regression into the existing Live Feed allocator build and added the bound index/progress paths as workflow triggers. GitHub Actions run 37024687124 completed the allocator-build step successfully with the new regression. Served-browser verification remains owned by the existing independent browser-verification surface and was not falsely claimed here.
